note: Remove Username has NO config, no configure route, no permissions, no Drush, no plugins and no config schema. Its behaviour is entirely hooks: form_alters that hide account][name and make mail required/relabel Username to 'Email address' on login+password forms, plus hook_user_presave that forces $user->setUsername($user->getEmail()) on every save. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that presave rule: creating/updating a user makes name == mail regardless of any requested username, verifiable with drush against the live user entity. All artifacts are namespaced with the ru_ / ru_*@example.com prefix.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site I enabled the remove_username module. What does it change on the user registration and account-edit forms, and what happens to a user's username when the account is saved?
evals.expected_output: It hides the separate Username field (account][name #access=FALSE) and makes the email field required on the register and edit forms, and hook_user_presave copies the email into the username (setUsername(getEmail())) on every save, so the username always equals the email.

evals.prompt: After enabling remove_username, does the login form still ask for a 'Username'? What does the module do to the login and forgotten-password forms specifically?
evals.expected_output: On user_login_form and user_pass the module does not hide the field; it only relabels the name field's #title to 'Email address'. Users log in by typing their email (which is also their username).

evals.prompt: Where is the settings page for remove_username, and how do I configure which forms it affects on a Drupal site?
evals.expected_output: There is no settings page and no configuration (configure is null, no permissions, no schema). Behaviour is fixed in hook_form_FORM_ID_alter implementations and hook_user_presave; to change or revert it you enable/uninstall the module or write your own hooks.

evals.prompt: A user account exists on this Drupal site with the email address ru_known@example.com. Because remove_username is enabled, inspect the live site and state that account's username (the 'name' value).
evals.expected_output: The username is ru_known@example.com — remove_username_user_presave() forced the name to equal the email even though the account was created with a different requested username.

evals.prompt: An account on this site was created with the email ru_known2@example.com and the requested username 'chosenhandle'. Inspect the live user entity and report what username it actually has now.
evals.expected_output: Its username is ru_known2@example.com, not 'chosenhandle': the presave hook overwrote the requested username with the email address.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (remove_username is enabled), create a new active user account for the email address ru_task@example.com, following the site's email-as-identity model so that the account's username matches its email. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A user exists whose mail is ru_task@example.com and whose name equals ru_task@example.com. Simply creating the user with that email is enough because remove_username_user_presave() sets the username to the email on save.

evals.prompt: On this site there is an account with email ru_task2@example.com. Change that account's email address to ru_new2@example.com and save it, making sure its username tracks the new email as remove_username requires. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: After the change, a user exists whose mail is ru_new2@example.com and whose name equals ru_new2@example.com, and no account with ru_task2@example.com remains. The presave hook copies the new email into the username automatically on save.
